Front: a horizontal card cage at the left under the PSU-shelf air intake - two CCM-e slots (A, B) then 4 MDA-e slots numbered 1/1 to 1/4 - with the integrated cable-management tray beside it and the hinged grill over the air filter at the right. Rear: the PSU shelf across the top (4 slots), the CPM-e slots A and B and 1 IOM-e slot at the left, and the chassis-specific fan tray standing in the vertical slot at the right. Every card lies horizontally, as the guide draws it, so no card bay rotates.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"Every figure used is vendor line art. Slot boundaries were read where one card's bottom edge meets the next card's top edge along x 200; they fall at a mean pitch of 35.29 mm, and the stack is laid out at the family's U = 35.4 (the conventions' pitch, measured 35.43 across the SR-3e's 14 slots) from y 46.1, which leaves every boundary within 0.5 mm of the drawing. Top to bottom: CCM A, CCM B, then MDA 1/1 onward."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"SR-e guide Table 21 (p79): 10.5 x 17.5 x 21.2 in (H x W x D), 6 RU; weight 23.8 kg unpopulated, 44.9 kg full. The table's note 2 says the 17.5 in width \"includes the integrated flanges\", but p89 Figure 25 dimensions it otherwise: \"Chassis Width 17.5 in (444.5 mm)\" between arrows that land on the body, and \"Chassis Flange Width 19 in (482.6 mm)\" over the ears, with hole centres 465 mm apart. Measured on that figure at 1200 dpi (9.948 px/mm from the 19 in flange), the body arrows sit 18.4 mm and 20.0 mm in from the flange edges. So the face is the 444.5 between the folds, the ears (about 19 mm a side, not drawn) carry the rack holes, and the note is read as loose wording. Depth 538.5 excludes panel protrusions (note 3)."},"colour":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"No photograph is staged; the charcoal chassis and grey trim are assumed. Those contracts are built on the sibling wave-1 branches (SR-e modules; MDA-e SFP; MDA-e 100G), so on this branch alone they do not resolve; they were checked against those branches' contracts before commit. Drawn as panel decor (a stud plate is chassis metalwork with no part number; no library part draws a two-stud earth point without its own symbol)."},"intake-door":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The hinged grill (key 6) frame x 301.6-437.7, y 50.4-256; opening y 62.6-243.6; louvres at y 80.7, 116.2, 151.7, 187.3, 216.1; handle (key 7) at y 137.4. p69 says the filter slot is \"angled slightly from left to right\"; the door is drawn flat, as the conventions ask (it carries no ports). The face frame used for every x below is the body centred on the flanges (face x = (px - centre)/8.587 + 222.25), y from the top outer edge.
